compiled_state.description:
Run the one-time reclaim. **Do not start until A1-A5, A6-0a..0d and Epic B's B6 are closed**,
A6-0b records a successful deployment/runtime receipt for the live review bot, and a completed
`reconcile-bridge.yml` run has a `github.sha` descending from the A6-0a merge. The epoch-blind
writer risk is closed by direct runtime proofs under quiescence, not by elapsed time. session_log
**1cb6-d553-6565-49b4** (measured facts; do not re-derive).

## Protocol
1. **Agent** disables `reconcile-bridge.yml` + `reconcile-bridge-canary.yml` (`gh workflow disable`,
   which also blocks `workflow_dispatch` and therefore `RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS` self-redispatch);
   **asserts** no reconcile run is in progress (poll `gh run list`, not drain-and-hope); polls the
   deployed review-bot `/health` until `in_flight == 0` and runs an authenticated Gerrit query for
   `status:open -label:LLM-Review`, requiring no current patchset that is still awaiting its vote.
   Zero sessions stops new pushes, but a patchset pushed just before the window can otherwise have
   its vote fire during it, and every vote writes a ticket; break-glasses
   `refs/reconciler/{lock,gate}` if held.
2. **Agent** pauses the AWS `rebar-autodeploy.timer` and the host LaunchAgents
   `com.navapbc.rebar-worktree-gc` (04:00) and `com.navapbc.rebar-dev-update`. It explicitly
   refreshes the host `rebar` installation from a descendant of the A6-0a merge, records the
   executable path and version/source, and executes an epoch-mismatch refusal probe with that exact
   runtime against temporary real clones. It also records the completed descendant
   `reconcile-bridge.yml` run and successful `git merge-base --is-ancestor` result. These direct
   observations replace the former 24-hour proxy and prevent the hourly updater from reverting the
   binary mid-window. **[operator-attested] Operator** confirms **zero active sessions** and all
   **`rebar-mcp` servers stopped** (a long-running MCP holds an in-process store handle and does
   not hot-reload). Gerrit needs no separate confirmation: every Gerrit push comes from a session.
3. **Agent** converges the local tracker (`fetch` + `reset --hard origin/tickets`, 0-ahead verified).
   This covers all 48 sibling worktrees at once — their `.tickets-tracker` are **symlinks to the one
   store**. The four other real trackers on the host point at different GitHub repos.
4. **Agent** deletes the pre-rewrite ref pins (A6-0d), runs the strip in a fresh **unfiltered** clone,
   verifies the pre-push assertions, and pushes with **`--force-with-lease`**.
5. **Agent** asserts non-resurrection: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip> origin/tickets` is
   **false**, and no clone-fetched ref has the old tip as an ancestor.
6. **Agent** converges the review-bot clone over SSM (`fetch && reset --hard origin/tickets` on
   `/var/gerrit/site/reviewbot-tickets`). Reverts to **[operator-attested]** if the issued AWS
   credentials do not permit `ssm send-command` against `i-00880b2c7f13527c5`.
7. **Agent** lands the `enforce_since` re-pin through Gerrit, mapped via the commit-map.
   The re-pinned key is `[identity].enforce_since` at `rebar.toml:115`, the only literal SHA in the
   system. With `require_authenticated = false` (`:106`) `verify_authorship.py:531-550` returns
   early and never reads it, so there is **no CI deadlock** and the change lands normally. The
   separate `[verify].opcert_enforce_since` key is unset.
8. **Agent** treats the Gerrit re-pin's review-bot vote as the deterministic first post-window
   write: records its change/patchset and vote timestamp, fetches `origin/tickets`, asserts
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip> origin/tickets` is false, and measures `size-pack`
   growth from the immediate post-rewrite baseline as < 1 MB.
9. **Agent** re-enables the GitHub workflows, the AWS timer, and both LaunchAgents.
10. **Agent** verifies the ACs below and **notifies the operator** that the tickets branch is
    available for sessions again.

## T11 migration-safety answers
- **Expand/contract:** yes — A6-0a's reader ships before the epoch value exists; the descendant
  workflow run, live review-bot refusal probe, and exact host-runtime refusal probe prove deployment
  directly while every writer is quiesced.
- **Batching:** n/a, single atomic ref update.
- **Resumability: NONE, stated.** A force-push is not resumable. Mitigation: all correctness
  assertions run on the scratch clone **before** publishing, so a wrong graph never reaches origin;
  the push itself is atomic per-ref.
- **Dual-write window:** none — the store is quiesced; the epoch guard replaces dual-write as the
  stale-writer defence.
- **Rollback:** restore from the A6-0d bundle + `--force-with-lease` back to the old tip. Known
  limit: rollback re-diverges anything already converged, so consumers must be re-converged in the
  same order as the forward path. **No event bytes are ever altered** — only commit SHAs — so the
  rewrite itself cannot lose ticket data.
- **T4 destructiveness:** an irreversible force-push to the authoritative store of a live system,
  chosen deliberately to reclaim 92% of the branch, gated on operator-confirmed quiescence, an
  off-repo bundle, a fail-closed epoch guard, and pre-push assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] [operator-attested] The A6-0a merge SHA, a completed descendant
      `reconcile-bridge.yml` run id, and successful ancestry result are recorded before publication.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A6-0b records the deployed review-bot SHA or image digest plus a live
      epoch-mismatch refusal result from that runtime.
- [ ] [operator-attested] The explicitly refreshed host executable path/version and its successful
      epoch-mismatch refusal result are recorded before publication.
- [ ] [operator-attested] A fresh **unfiltered** clone of `tickets` is **<=150 MB** (from 1.04 GiB; the measured strip
      result is ~94 MiB) and `rev-parse HEAD^{tree}` equals the recorded pre-rewrite tip tree.
      **Holds only because B6 landed first.** Tier: **repo-level measurement**.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Commit count and merge-commit count on `tickets` are **unchanged** versus the pre-rewrite
      recording (measured at window time, never hardcoded). Tier: **repo assertion**.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar verify-identity --require-authenticated --since <sha> --format json`, run pre-rewrite
      against the old SHA and post-rewrite against the mapped SHA: the **stderr summary counts** are
      identical AND the multiset of `(event_uuid, verdict, grandfathered)` from the JSON report is
      identical **ignoring `commit`**. (JSON mode puts only the report array on stdout and the summary
      on stderr; the report lists only non-verified events; every `commit` is a rewritten SHA. The
      command **exits 1** when `enforced_not_verified > 0`, so do not require exit 0.) Tier: **CLI
      subprocess, both sides**.
- [ ] [operator-attested] After the review bot's first post-window write, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <old-tip>
      origin/tickets` is **false** and `size-pack` growth is **< 1 MB**. The ancestry assertion is
      what actually proves non-resurrection. Tier: **repo measurement after an observed vote**.
- [ ] [operator-attested] No ref a default clone fetches has the old tip as an ancestor. Tier: `ls-remote` +
      `merge-base` loop, computed at window time.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Operator confirmation of zero active sessions and stopped MCP servers is
      recorded as a comment before step 3.
- [ ] [code-verifiable] The landed `rebar.toml` `identity.enforce_since` value equals the
      mapped post-rewrite SHA derived from the pre-window pin.
- [ ] [operator-attested] Post-enable reconciliation is validated by either a green reconcile-bridge.yml run or, during a GitHub Actions outage, an operator-approved production-equivalent signed CLI sequence: pre-live dry-run with zero mutation/recovery failures; live pass(es) exit 0 with every Jira batch error=None and silent_noop=[]; persisted state is pushed; final dry-run has zero mutation/recovery failures; and the canary classifier reports drift_total=0. Tier: **CLI subprocess**.
- [ ] [operator-attested] `rebar fsck` is clean after step 9. Tier: **CLI subprocess**.

## Files
Operational — no `src/` changes. Uses the A6-0c script and A6-0d helpers; touches `rebar.toml`
(`identity.enforce_since`) via Gerrit in step 7.

Scope: M (operational). Direct dependencies: A5, A6-0b (which depends on A6-0a), A6-0c, and
A6-0d. A1-A4 and Epic B's B6 are transitive/epic start gates and must also be closed.
